newsitem.title: USA: WSCC group proposes 6,900 MW summer Intertie limit.
newsitem.headline: WSCC group proposes 6,900 MW summer Intertie limit.

text.p: A technical committee is proposing a summertime rating for the Pacific Intertie of 6,900 megawatts (MW), compared with the current springtime limit of 7,200 MW, sources involved in the rating studies said Wednesday.
A special study group convened by the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) will pass its recommendations to the WSCC board next week.
Under WSCC operating criteria, the current rate remains in effect until regional streamflows slow down after the spring melt.

Sources said the lower summer limit is a reflection of reliability concerns related to the large volumes of southbound power that typically flow along the interstate transmission system during hot summer months.
